intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF5B gene (602809) on chromosome 10p11.

checks.claim: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type (KDII) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KIF5B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings suggest that heterozygous KIF5B deleterious variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The paper states that heterozygous KIF5B variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia. The name 'Itai-Ikegawa type' is the draft's own label.

checks.claim: The KIF5B gene is located on chromosome 10p11.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B encoding kinesin-1 heavy chain
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't give the chromosomal location, but standard gene location nomenclature counts as supported under the rules.

paragraphs.text: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, is a skeletal dysplasia defined mainly by marked angulation (kyphomelia) of the long bones, especially the femora, together with short stature. It is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in the kinesin heavy chain gene KIF5B.

checks.claim: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, is a skeletal dysplasia defined mainly by marked angulation (kyphomelia) of the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: Kyphomelic dysplasia is a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias characterized by severe bowing of the limbs
checks.explanation: The paper defines the disorder by severe limb bowing, and all patients had sharp angulation of long bones.

checks.claim: In kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, the long-bone angulation especially affects the femora.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri
checks.explanation: The femora are involved, but the paper names femora and humeri equally and doesn't say the femora are especially affected.

checks.claim: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, is characterized by short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: kyphomelic dysplasia, a skeletal dysplasia characterized by short stature, narrow thorax, bowing of the long bones and dysmorphic craniofacial features.

checks.claim: Kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in KIF5B.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B encoding kinesin-1 heavy chain

checks.claim: KIF5B is a kinesin heavy chain gene.

paragraphs.text: The eponym refers to Itai and Ikegawa, the first and senior authors of the report that linked this form of kyphomelic dysplasia to KIF5B. It distinguishes the disorder from other conditions that have been called kyphomelic dysplasia.

checks.claim: Itai and Ikegawa were the first and senior authors of the report that linked kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, to KIF5B.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no author list, so it can't confirm that Ikegawa was the senior author.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) reported a small number of unrelated patients with kyphomelic dysplasia. The main features were bowing and angulation of the long bones, most obvious in the femora, and short stature.

checks.claim: Itai et al. (2022) reported a small number of unrelated patients with kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Four individuals diagnosed with kyphomelic dysplasia were enrolled.
checks.explanation: Four patients were reported, but the abstract doesn't say they were unrelated.

checks.claim: The main features of the kyphomelic dysplasia patients reported by Itai et al. (2022) were bowing and angulation of the long bones.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress.
checks.explanation: Long-bone angulation was present in all patients.

checks.claim: In the kyphomelic dysplasia patients reported by Itai et al. (2022), long-bone bowing and angulation was most obvious in the femora.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri
checks.explanation: The paper reports femoral and humeral angulation together and doesn't say the femora were most affected.

checks.claim: Short stature was a main feature of the kyphomelic dysplasia patients reported by Itai et al. (2022).
checks.evidence_quote: Short stature was observed in three individuals.
checks.explanation: Only three of the four patients had short stature.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous KIF5B mutations reported by Itai et al. (2022) arose de novo, which fits autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The heterozygous KIF5B mutations reported by Itai et al. (2022) in kyphomelic dysplasia patients arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals had de novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B

checks.claim: The de novo heterozygous KIF5B mutations in kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai-Ikegawa type, are consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings suggest that heterozygous KIF5B deleterious variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The paper doesn't use the words 'autosomal dominant', but this follows directly from de novo heterozygous variants causing the disorder.

paragraphs.text: Itai et al. (2022) used exome sequencing to study unrelated patients with kyphomelic dysplasia. They found de novo heterozygous missense mutations in the KIF5B gene, and the mutations clustered in the motor domain of the protein.

checks.claim: Itai et al. (2022) used exome sequencing to study unrelated patients with kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Four individuals diagnosed with kyphomelic dysplasia were enrolled. We performed whole-exome sequencing
checks.explanation: Exome sequencing is confirmed, but the abstract doesn't say the patients were unrelated.

checks.claim: Itai et al. (2022) found de novo heterozygous missense mutations in the KIF5B gene in patients with kyphomelic dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: two with c.272A>G:p.(Lys91Arg), one with c.584C>A:p.(Thr195Lys), and the other with c.701G>T:p.(Gly234Val)
checks.explanation: All the de novo heterozygous variants are amino acid substitutions, so they are missense.

checks.claim: The KIF5B missense mutations identified by Itai et al. (2022) in kyphomelic dysplasia patients clustered in the motor domain of the KIF5B protein.
checks.evidence_quote: All variants involved conserved amino acids in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs in the catalytic motor domain of the KIF5B protein.

references.label: Itai et al. (2022)
references.citation: Itai T, Wang Z, Nishimura G, Ohashi H, Guo L, Wakano Y, Sugiura T, Hayakawa H, Okada M, Saisu T, and others. De novo heterozygous variants in KIF5B cause kyphomelic dysplasia. Clin Genet 102: 3-11, 2022. [PubMed: 35342932]
